scenarios.title: The aged balance trapped in a print file
scenarios.goal: Turn a paginated accounting print file into receivables per invoice, keeping the right client across page breaks and dropping headers and totals.

scenarios.title: An application inventory with hand-typed URLs
scenarios.goal: Split each URL into server, port and environment, to know what runs on a server and what is still in staging.

scenarios.title: AS/400: the customer over its credit limit, read in EBCDIC
scenarios.goal: Read an IBM i customer master in its French EBCDIC, and be told when a customer's outstanding balance exceeds its credit limit.

scenarios.title: Failed orders hidden in the logs
scenarios.goal: Tie each error in the application log to its order, its customer and its current status, to know which customers to call back.

scenarios.title: The wrong bar code caught at import
scenarios.goal: Catch wrong bar codes at import.
scenarios.lede:
A catalogue export carries EAN-13 bar codes, some of them wrong. No built-in transformer computes the check digit.
- the hub's operator drops a Kotlin script
- the manifest names it, carrying no code
- a draft that does not compile is refused at validation
- every code gets a verdict at import.

scenarios.title: A CFONB statement with the sign hidden in the last digit
scenarios.goal: Read the CFONB 120 bank statement as a table: every movement signed, tied to its statement, with its payer and invoice.

scenarios.title: The freezer probe reads 6.8 °C in the middle of the night
scenarios.goal: Be alerted as soon as an independent HACCP probe sees a freezer above -18 °C, even when the refrigeration controller says nothing.
scenarios.lede:
In autumn 2026, supermarket refrigeration controllers were changed remotely. In France, on 11 October, no alarm went off. An independent HACCP probe measures the temperature, and ChirpStack publishes its readings to Kafka.
- the reading is nested in the event: promote turns it into a column
- a registry says which cabinet, which aisle, who is on call
- at 02:30, PROBE-07 reads 6.8 °C: one decision

scenarios.title: HPLC report: the impurity over its limit, read from the instrument's export
scenarios.goal: Read the injection reports an HPLC exports, units glued and decimal commas, and be told when an impurity exceeds its specification.

scenarios.title: A CRM export with broken accents and wrong emails
scenarios.goal: Take over the old CRM's contacts with a repaired name, an international phone and a valid email, and name those that cannot be reached.

scenarios.title: The €240,000 deal that confirms itself during dinner
scenarios.goal: Tell the sales engineer on their phone as soon as the CRM marks a deal ready to confirm, with the line, the parts and the catalogue at hand, and have one tap on Traiter move the CRM and send the customer email.

scenarios.title: A delivery date each warehouse works out differently
scenarios.goal: Promise the customer the date their warehouse can keep: one calculation rule, set per warehouse (country, lead time, closed days).
scenarios.lede:
The promised date = order date plus N working days. But each warehouse counts its own way:
- Lyon, in France: 3 days, two inventory days;
- Liège, in Belgium: 5 days, other holidays.
The operator writes the rule once; the integrator sets it per warehouse.

scenarios.title: k8s forgot its events and lumnik still knows who crashed last night
scenarios.goal: Ask which deployments crashed in a loop after Kubernetes erased their events, and get the list kubectl gave during the incident.
scenarios.lede:
Kubernetes keeps its events for one hour. A deployment repaired at dawn has no history by morning:
- a new pod, Running, 0 restarts;
- no Warning event left.
lumnik reads the events while they exist and keeps them; Ask still answers when kubectl no longer knows.

scenarios.title: k9s says Running while the cluster burns: which pod first?
scenarios.goal: Ask your Kubernetes cluster which pods to handle first, and get the list ordered by the on-call rule, checked against kubectl.

scenarios.title: An unapproved hotfix in k8s prod stops the pipeline
scenarios.goal: Block a release when a pod runs a version the release board did not approve, with an exit code a CI understands.

scenarios.title: One order status spelled fourteen ways
scenarios.goal: Count orders by status whatever the spelling, and be told of a new spelling.
scenarios.lede:
Fifteen years of hand entry left EC, Livré, LIV, ANNUL… in the ERP's order export. lumnik does not touch the ERP:
- a Workflow declares four statuses and their spellings
- every import re-checks the column.

scenarios.title: The order lines of a flat EDI file read at their place
scenarios.goal: Read the order lines of a fixed-width EDI file as columns, with no mapping tool.

scenarios.title: Four EDI files for a single order line
scenarios.goal: Merge the four flows to know whether each line is ordered, confirmed or delivered, and be alerted when a confirmed date passes without delivery.
scenarios.lede:
A manufacturer and its logistics partner exchange four flat files around one order line: the order, the acknowledgement, the confirmed date, the delivery note. Sales administration asks, line by line:
- never acknowledged?
- confirmed but not delivered?
- delivered in another quantity?

scenarios.title: An EDIFACT ORDERS message read again order line by order line
scenarios.goal: Read an EDIFACT order segment by segment, then line by line, with no EDI tool.

scenarios.title: One customer in two systems with no shared id
scenarios.goal: Match ERP customers and CRM contacts, without ever merging by chance.

scenarios.title: An established customer does not switch records in silence
scenarios.goal: See when a CRM contact starts pointing at another customer, instead of moving it in silence.

scenarios.title: Every line of the Excel export gets its region and its client back
scenarios.goal: Read an Excel report with merged cells as a table, one row per sale.

scenarios.title: An unreadable line of the export does not pass in silence
scenarios.goal: Never write or remove half a catalogue when one of its lines is unreadable.

scenarios.title: Firebird (Delphi): refused over JDBC, read through its export
scenarios.goal: Read a Delphi application's Firebird database, and be told when an article falls under its reorder threshold.

scenarios.title: A critical incident is left without a technician
scenarios.goal: Warn the maintenance manager as soon as a critical incident has no technician.
scenarios.lede:
A CMMS exports its incidents as CSV. The conveyor on the gummy candy line has stopped, with no technician. The CMMS warns no one.
- a Workflow tracks each incident's status
- a Process flags the critical unassigned incident
- one decision only; the assignment moves it forward.

scenarios.title: A claim form's lists come from the CRM without exposing its GraphQL
scenarios.goal: Feed a form's lists from a GraphQL CRM without the browser depending on the CRM's schema.
scenarios.lede:
The claim type and subtype live in a CRM that speaks GraphQL. lumnik ingests it page by page into a canonical entity.
- a small BFF serves the form stable REST JSON
- switching from Car to Home replaces the list
- an unknown type answers 404

scenarios.title: HL7 v2: the analyser result above its range, flagged or not
scenarios.goal: Read the HL7 v2 messages two analysers drop for the LIMS, and be told when a result is above its reference range.

scenarios.title: The catalogue leaves for the partner in the partner's format
scenarios.goal: Deliver the product catalogue to a partner in the format it imposes, with no conversion code.
scenarios.lede:
Two CSV files from an ERP, products and categories, are joined in the hub and delivered to S3 in a partner's format.
- French headers, semicolons, decimal commas
- recoded statuses, masked internal reference
- a receipt proves the delivered bytes

scenarios.title: An invoice with an unreadable amount waits for its fix at the source
scenarios.goal: Never write an invoice without an amount, and follow each set-aside line until it is fixed.

scenarios.title: One product record joins PostgreSQL and Oracle with nothing migrated
scenarios.goal: Show a complete product record when the product lives in PostgreSQL and its category in Oracle, without touching either database.
scenarios.lede:
Products live in PostgreSQL, their categories in Oracle. Two jdbc connectors read them without writing anything, and an entity joins them.
- 40,234 products, 63 categories
- each product carries its category when there is one
- the product with no category stays, with empty fields

scenarios.title: Lyon draws 18.7 kW at night and only its owner is alerted
scenarios.goal: Be alerted when a closed site draws more than its night threshold, without alerting the sites where that load is normal.
scenarios.lede:
Three meters publish their power to Kafka at 23:15. A CSV registry says what each site is.
- Lyon draws 18.7 kW against a 10 kW threshold: one decision, one email
- the laboratory draws 28.4 kW, under its 40 kW threshold: nothing
- Grafana follows all three states

scenarios.title: An open freezer door and a silent sensor
scenarios.goal: Be alerted when a freezer door stays open past one minute, with the laboratory and the owner.
scenarios.lede:
Sensors publish freezer door states on Kafka. FZ-17 opens and goes quiet. FZ-18 opens and closes again.
- a Workflow watches the silence
- one alert only, for the door left open past one minute
- it names the laboratory and the owner.

scenarios.title: A frozen ERP feeds a real Grafana dashboard
scenarios.goal: Give management an up-to-date sales dashboard from the exports of an ERP nobody touches any more.
scenarios.lede:
The ERP exports its sales and its catalogue as CSV. lumnik joins them, and Grafana reads the entity through a read-only PostgreSQL account, bounded to its tenant.
- Monday: €10,450
- Tuesday, the export changes: €14,200
- the changed sale appears once

scenarios.title: Expired calibrations: the results measured on an out-of-date instrument
scenarios.goal: Flag every lab result measured outside its instrument's calibration validity (ISO 17025), from the register and the LIMS as they export.

scenarios.title: One row per item to pick with model colour and size
scenarios.goal: Turn a marketplace export into one row per item, to pick the stock.

scenarios.title: A technician sees only the maintenance app
scenarios.goal: Give each business line its app on the same hub, without a technician being able to read purchasing's data.
scenarios.lede:
Maintenance and purchasing share an ERP where everyone sees everything. On the same hub, lumnik composes one app per business line.
- the technician holds only the Keycloak role scope:maintenance
- they see their app, their orders and their decisions
- every purchasing door answers with a refusal

scenarios.title: Auditing how long orders stay in each status
scenarios.goal: Know how long each order stays in each status, and which ones stop moving.
scenarios.lede:
The ERP keeps only today's status: In progress yesterday, Delivered today. Nothing on the wait in between. The ERP cannot be changed.
- a Workflow follows each order by its key
- each status change enters a journal, dated
- an order that stays still too long alerts
- the journal says how long each order stayed in each state.

scenarios.title: Ask refuses a margin with no cost and a best supplier with no criterion
scenarios.goal: Let a purchasing director question their orders in their own words, without being handed a figure the data does not hold.
scenarios.lede:
A purchasing director asks questions of a year of supplier orders. Three questions get their figure, with the SQL that produced it.
- a margin with no cost price: refused
- a best supplier with no criterion: refused
- delays with no delivery date: refused

scenarios.title: And SUP-004? Ask answers the follow-up as the whole question
scenarios.goal: Let a buyer chain questions without retyping them, showing each time the question understood.
scenarios.lede:
A buyer asks how many orders were cancelled, then "And for supplier SUP-003?", then "And SUP-004?". They do not retype the question.
- Ask reads each follow-up with the question before
- it answers the full question and shows it
- a follow-up the data cannot answer is refused

scenarios.title: Question 40,000 items in French and see the SQL
scenarios.goal: Let a user question the catalogue in their own words, without learning the columns or writing SQL.
scenarios.lede:
Two CSV exports, one entity, an app reduced to chat. The question becomes a read-only query.
- 40,233 items, each with its category
- "How many items in the Pompes category?": 7,407
- the answer shows its SQL

scenarios.title: 40,000 items browsed page by page in the PWA
scenarios.goal: Browse a whole catalogue in the PWA without ever loading more than 50 rows at a time.
scenarios.lede:
Two CSV exports, two entities, two linked views, one app. The hub serves the catalogue in pages of 50.
- 40,233 items reached, no duplicate
- categories linked both ways
- the Open edition is enough

scenarios.title: Search 40,000 items with facets in the PWA
scenarios.goal: Find an item by its words or the start of its reference, and narrow by category, in the PWA.
scenarios.lede:
Two CSV exports, one entity, a SearchIndex, an app reduced to search.
- "Pompes": 7,407 items, 6,761 active
- "Pompe Badu": 122 inactive
- the hub indexes the declared columns only

scenarios.title: One unexpected value in 500 as a dead letter and the other 499 written
scenarios.goal: Keep one unexpected line from stopping the other 499, and keep it visible.

scenarios.title: The carrier wants its cursor in a header or the run fails
scenarios.goal: Read every tracking event of a carrier whose API expects the page cursor in a request header.

scenarios.title: Drupal: the whole site read through JSON:API in one line
scenarios.goal: Read every article of a Drupal site through its JSON:API module, without writing the paging.

scenarios.title: FastAPI: 130 deliveries read in one line
scenarios.goal: Read every delivery of an in-house FastAPI service through its API, without asking its team for an export.

scenarios.title: An order changed during the read is not lost
scenarios.goal: Read only what changed each night, without losing what changes during the read.

scenarios.title: An old app behind a login: lumnik logs in like a user
scenarios.goal: Read the vets of Spring PetClinic, protected by the Tomcat server's login, without touching the app.

scenarios.title: An old Spring MVC app returns the whole list at once and one line reads it
scenarios.goal: Read the vets of Spring PetClinic, a Spring MVC app from before Spring Boot, without touching its code.

scenarios.title: A ticket closed in Gitea stays open in the hub if only open ones are read
scenarios.goal: Follow a Gitea forge's open tickets, paged by its Link header, without keeping open a ticket support has closed.

scenarios.title: Micronaut: the stores' parts read in three requests
scenarios.goal: Read every spare part of a Micronaut service through its API, even while the stores work in it.

scenarios.title: NestJS: a ticket deleted mid-read no longer costs its neighbour
scenarios.goal: Read every ticket of a NestJS service through its API, even while the support team works in it.

scenarios.title: NetBox: the whole network inventory read with a read-only token
scenarios.goal: Read every device of a NetBox, the network team's source of truth, each night, with a read-only token.

scenarios.title: Paperless-ngx: a list that moves while it is read is read again
scenarios.goal: Read every correspondent of a Paperless-ngx archive through its API, even while someone works in it.

scenarios.title: The partner's API loses a page and the run does not lie
scenarios.goal: Never let a run call itself complete when the source served fewer rows than it declares.

scenarios.title: PrestaShop: the XML catalogue read in one line
scenarios.goal: Read every product of a PrestaShop 8 shop through its Webservice, in XML, as it answers.

scenarios.title: Sequelize: the service announces 260 orders for 130
scenarios.goal: Read every order of a Node service through its API without believing a wrong total.

scenarios.title: A Spring app behind a proxy keeps each product under its SKU
scenarios.goal: Read a home-grown Spring Data REST application's whole stock, page by page, and keep each product under its SKU, whatever host it is reached through.

scenarios.title: Spring changes its page JSON and one line follows
scenarios.goal: Read a Spring Boot app's whole catalogue, page after page, before and after the team changes how its Pages are serialized.

scenarios.title: Spring Slice: an article deleted mid-read lands on no page
scenarios.goal: Read every article of a Spring Boot catalogue through its API, and know when one may be missing.

scenarios.title: Stripe: every customer read without writing the pagination
scenarios.goal: Read every customer of a Stripe account, page after page, without writing the paging.

scenarios.title: WordPress announces 46 articles and serves 31: the run fails
scenarios.goal: Read every article of a WordPress site, and refuse a partial read when a plugin hides some without changing the count.

scenarios.title: The SaaS behind OAuth2 read without losing a page
scenarios.goal: Read an OAuth2-protected SaaS without losing a page, and say why when access is refused.

scenarios.title: Every line of a SAP ORDERS05 IDoc gets its customer order back
scenarios.goal: Read a SAP customer's order IDocs, one row per order line, with no middleware.

scenarios.title: SAP OData v2: the 48,000 EUR order left unprocessed
scenarios.goal: Read SAP's sales orders through the OData v2 Gateway, then be told when a large order stays unprocessed.

scenarios.title: SENAITE: Fleming's plate waiting to be verified
scenarios.goal: Be told when a SENAITE LIMS result goes over its limit, then when nobody verifies it.

scenarios.title: The carrier's SFTP drop read every night with nothing taken on trust
scenarios.goal: Read the carrier's file every night, file it away, and refuse a server whose key changed.

scenarios.title: Every order says which version of the rule computed it
scenarios.goal: Know, months later, which shipping rule computed each order.

scenarios.title: The CRM's SOAP desk read service by service with nothing read twice
scenarios.goal: Read an old CRM's SOAP services, each as it reads, without hammering it.

scenarios.title: A changed bank account the SIEM never sees
scenarios.goal: Let the SIEM see a supplier's IBAN change, without the IBAN showing in the inbox.
scenarios.lede:
The ERP exports its suppliers as CSV. It emits no event. A bank-account change goes unnoticed until the next payment.
- lumnik rereads the export every minute
- a signed decision goes to the SIEM by webhook
- the SIEM alerts on the account that changes
- the inbox never shows the account.

scenarios.title: The supplier file goes to EDI in ASCII with a stable id
scenarios.goal: Send EDI the suppliers in the form it requires, with an id that does not change.

scenarios.title: Two systems and one member each one rules its own fields
scenarios.goal: Show each field of a member from the system that rules it, without hiding a disagreement.

scenarios.title: Two customers write to the same table and each reads only their own rows
scenarios.goal: Host two customers on one hub without either being able to read, count or open the other's data.
scenarios.lede:
Two integrators of two customers apply the same files on the same hub: same connector, same entity, same table. Each loads their orders, under the same numbers.
- each reads back 240 or 60 rows, never the other's
- the same question gives the same SQL and two answers
- the other's run answers 404

scenarios.title: WinDev: the client export with real dates and a real Active flag
scenarios.goal: Read the client file a WinDev application exports, and turn it into columns a question can use.

scenarios.title: The CMMS is switched off and the hub still returns the same bytes
scenarios.goal: Switch off a replaced CMMS without losing its thirty years of work orders or its compliance reads.
scenarios.lede:
A replaced CMMS stays on for a few compliance reads a year. lumnik reads it one last time, archives what it read, and the machine is switched off.
- 3,600 orders read by the usual schedule
- one S3 archive under one digest
- after the switch-off: the same row, the same bytes
